contradictions.fact: High camp: Camp Muir vs camps below it on the traverse

claims.says: Camp Muir
From here the route traverses east across the Cowlitz and Ingraham glaciers to Little Tahoma.
You step off the Camp Muir track while still about 1,500 ft BELOW Camp Muir. IF YOU REACH CAMP MUIR YOU HAVE GONE TOO FAR
Camp is commonly made on the Cowlitz or Ingraham glacier, or on the more exposed Cathedral Rocks cleaver.
approach from Paradise to a camp on the Cowlitz/Ingraham glacier or Cathedral Rocks cleaver

contradictions.why: The only camp card sends parties to Camp Muir and says the traverse leaves from there, but the approach says the traverse leaves the Muir track at 8,600 ft and that reaching Camp Muir means you have gone too far.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, approach_variants, beta, pro_tips and itinerary all agree: leave the Muir route at ~8,600 ft and camp on the Cowlitz/Ingraham glacier or the Cathedral Rocks cleaver. The Camp Muir bivy entry is the outlier.

claims.says: Jul-Sep (best early July-early Aug while glaciers are well-filled and rock is more often frozen)
June-early August

contradictions.why: Seasonal guidance calls June the prime window, which is outside the Jul-Sep season, and the road to the trailhead usually isn't open until late June or early July.
contradictions.internal_resolution: season, best_season, pro_tips and the road opening date all put the window at July onward; the June 'optimal' rating is the outlier.
